# Rule B1: Play a Realistic Character
You must roleplay a character that is believable and acts as if they are in the setting they exist in. Your character's actions, feelings and knowledge should be solely those of your character, and not your own as a player.
- [bold]Act in character throughout the round[/bold], and focus on collaborating with others to advance the story. Whether you do something should be based on whether it makes sense for your character to do such. - [bold]Do not play a ‘master of everything’ character[/bold]. Interact with other players, ask for assistance and negotiate as needed. It makes the world feel larger when you work with others. - [bold]Do not annoy, pester, or in any way harass other players[/bold] without any roleplay or IC reason to be doing so. - [bold]Actions that have no regard for your character's health and safety aren’t acceptable[/bold]. Act to threats made as if they are legitimate threats, and preserve yourself realistically. [italic](Don’t jump into space for a few moments just because a medbed will fix you up!)[/italic] -- Do not roleplay suicide in such a way it will alert Medical Responders. -- Roleplaying insanity or mental illness as an excuse to bypass this is not allowed.
## Rule B1.1: Following Naming Conventions In-character names must not make obvious references nor be a play on words, and must not be obscene. You're in the Zekke Sector, after all! Try and have fun with it. - [bold]Do not name yourself after another players character[/bold], do not attempt to impersonate anyone. - [bold]Ships follow the same naming conventions[/bold], although you have greater freedom with making references and plays on words. -- For example, there's leeway towards renaming your Shuttle IFF to "[italic]Behir Boykisser[/italic]", but don't name it something like "[italic]Ohio Rizz :3[/italic]".
[italic](NOTE: Don't be afraid to ask! If you want to have a name that you think may not be allowed, ask an admin for clarification, be it through an aHelp or otherwise. They can confirm if it’s fine!)[/italic]
## Rule B1.2: Communicate in Character Communicate as your character would, and use the emotes channels to describe your character’s physical movements. This allows using the emotes channels for talking in such manners as writing in books, typing into your PDA or otherwise. - [bold]Avoid use of Netspeak[/bold] [italic](i.e lol, fr, smh, :3, etc.)[/italic] outside of Nanochat, such that it might break immersion. - [bold]Do not engage in meta-communications[/bold] [italic](via Discord, OOC or other third party software)[/italic] if said communication is to gain an advantage.
## Rule B1.3: New Life Rules Sometimes people will die, these rules aid in Outlaws not being immediately unveiled if they are attempting to keep themselves a secret. When you die: - [bold]You are unaware of all things that happened whilst you were crit/dead/ghosted[/bold], and must not act upon this metaknowledge. - [bold]If you are revived within the round, your character will struggle to remember anything beyond vague elements[/bold]. “They had a laser sword” or “A large person was shooting at me”. -- This includes not naming your killer directly. - [bold]If you are Round Removed (RR), you may not join the round again with the same character[/bold]. The only exception for this is if you are RRed via personal scenes [italic](eg. Kink scenes)[/italic]. -- You are allowed to still play a Round Removed character in the following shift! They could have reformed, cloned, or be from a different dimension. If you're unsure, you can always ask an admin for help!
## Rule B1.4: Escalate Appropriately The priority of the server is to roleplay and tell a story, not to win. - [bold]Have an in-character justification for your actions and attacking others[/bold]. The level of escalation allowed proportionate to the level of roleplay invested. -- Although this will depend upon the situation, killing vermin on your ship needs no more justification than “it was vermin on my ship.” - [bold]Escalate a situation appropriate as your character would[/bold], keeping in mind that space is a dangerous place and killing anyone should be a last resort. - [bold]Do not attack another player without a legitimate, explainable roleplay reason[/bold] that could be applied in a similar, real-life scenario. - [bold]Do not "soft RR" someone[/bold]. If a fight results in someone being critically injured or killed, do not take steps to try and prevent a player from being revived, such as removing sensors and leaving them in an unreachable space, or unnecessarily guarding the body for long periods of time. -- This does not mean you can expect to retrieve a body without harm as a medic, especially in a hostile engagement.
